density-land-use-s1.title: Residential density by distance from the center in two cities

plot.label: Line chart: homes per hectare by distance from the city center in City 1 and City 2. Both lines fall with distance; City 1 stays much higher than City 2 at every distance.

density-land-use-s2.title: A city planning notice
density-land-use-s2.text: Invented notice for practice, 2026. "The city will hold a public hearing on a plan to build a five-story building with 60 apartments and a corner grocery on the empty lot at 4th Street and Oak Avenue, a parking lot since a factory closed there in 1998. The lot is zoned for factories and must be rezoned for homes and shops. The block is lined with two-story houses. Supporters say the plan will add homes near the bus line. Some neighbors say a five-story building is too tall for the block and will bring more traffic."

items.q: Which statement best describes the data in the chart?
options: Both fall with distance; City 1 stays denser
Density rises with distance from the center in both of the cities
City 2 is denser than City 1 near the center but not farther out
The two cities reach the same density by about 10 km from the center

why.correct: Both lines slope down, and City 1's line is above City 2's at every distance (120 vs 60 at the center, 40 vs 5 at 10 km).
options: Right: both fall, and City 1 stays higher.
Both lines slope downward.
At the center, City 1 has 120 homes per hectare and City 2 has 60.
At 10 km, City 1 has 40 and City 2 has 5.

items.q: Between the center and 4 km out, by how much does City 2's density fall compared with City 1's?
options: City 2 falls by 15 homes per hectare, City 1 by 85
Both fall by the same amount, about 40 homes per hectare
City 2 rises over this stretch while City 1 falls
City 2 falls by 45, City 1 by 35

why.correct: City 2: 60 to 15, a fall of 45. City 1: 120 to 85, a fall of 35. City 2 drops faster near the center.
options: Those are the values at 4 km, not the falls.
The falls are 45 and 35, not equal.
Both lines fall over this stretch.

items.q: City 2 grew mostly after 1950, when most families owned cars. City 1 grew mostly before 1900. Which best explains the difference in the chart?
options: City 1 had more cars than City 2, so it could afford to build higher
Streetcars made City 2 denser at its edge than near its center
Cars let City 2 spread out on cheap land
Elevators lowered density in City 1's center by spacing out its towers

why.correct: Before cars, people had to live within walking or streetcar distance of work, so City 1 packed homes close together. Cars let City 2 spread out at low density.
options: City 1 grew before most people owned cars.
Streetcars raise density along their lines, and City 2 grew after the car.
Right: car-era growth spreads homes out at low density.
Elevators raise density by allowing taller buildings.

items.q: Which term best describes the plan in the notice?
options: Urban sprawl
Infilling
Suburbanization
A squatter settlement

why.correct: Building on an empty lot inside an area already built up is infilling.
options: Sprawl spreads onto open land at the edge.
Right: new building on an empty lot inside the city.
Suburbanization moves people out of the central city.
The plan is a legal building approved by the city.

items.q: Why must the lot be rezoned before the building can go up?
options: It is zoned for factories
Its zoning sets a minimum height of five stories for any building
Its zoning keeps the lot as a parking lot for the old factory
The grocery store on the corner needs a farm permit first

why.correct: Zoning says what can be built on each lot. This lot is zoned for factories, so homes and a grocery are not allowed until the zone changes.
options: Right: the planned uses do not match the lot's zone.
The notice says nothing about a height minimum.
The lot is zoned for factories, not kept empty by law.
A grocery is a shop, not a farm.

items.q: What would the plan most likely do to the block's residential density?
options: Lower it, by replacing houses with a store
Leave it unchanged, because the lot was empty
Lower it, by adding a parking lot
Raise it, by adding 60 homes on one lot

why.correct: Sixty apartments on a lot with no homes adds many housing units to the same area, so homes per hectare rise.
options: No houses are torn down; the lot is a parking lot.
Adding homes to an empty lot changes the density of the block.
The plan replaces a parking lot with homes.
Right: more homes on the same land means higher density.

items.q: Which statement fairly describes the debate in the notice?
options: People on the block agree, so the public hearing is just a formality
Neighbors want the city to bring more factories back to the lot
Homes near a bus line versus height and traffic
Supporters want the lot kept as parking for the bus line riders

why.correct: The notice gives both sides: homes near a bus line versus a building taller than the block and more traffic.
options: The notice reports neighbors who disagree.
No one in the notice asks for factories.
Right: both sides, each with its reason.
The supporters favor the apartment plan.

items.q: Which neighborhood has the highest residential density?
options: Detached houses, each on a large lot with a yard
Six-story apartment blocks
Farms with one farmhouse on each farm
A shopping mall with a large parking lot

why.correct: Residential density counts homes on an area of land. Apartment blocks put the most homes on each hectare.
options: Large lots mean few homes per hectare.
Right: many homes stacked on each lot.
One house per farm is very low density.
A mall has few or no homes.

items.q: Houses in the old medina of Fez, Morocco, face inward onto private courtyards and have few windows on the street. Which influence on housing does this best show?
options: Culture, in a value placed on family privacy
Technology, in the use of steel and elevators
Zoning, in a rule that sets building heights
Cycles of development, in the decline of an old area

why.correct: The inward-facing courtyard form expresses a cultural value: privacy for the family from the street.
options: Right: the form of the home reflects cultural values.
Courtyard homes are old, low buildings, not steel towers.
The design comes from culture, not from a modern height rule.
The question is about the form of homes, not decline.

items.q: Steel frames and safe passenger elevators spread in New York and Chicago in the late 1800s. What effect did they have on land use near the CBD?
options: Lower buildings, so the density near the center fell
Factories moved out of the suburbs into the center
Homes spread out into suburbs on large lots
Taller buildings and higher density

why.correct: People no longer had to climb stairs, so buildings rose far higher, packing more offices and homes on each lot.
options: Elevators allowed taller, not lower, buildings.
Elevators did not move factories downtown.
Spreading out came later, with cars.
Right: technology let cities build upward.

items.q: Detroit lost more than half its population between the 1950 and 2020 US censuses, and many houses were torn down. Which stage of the cycle of development does this show?
options: Infilling, adding new homes on empty lots
Early growth of new homes on open farmland
Decline, leaving vacant land
The rise of a new CBD on the edge of the city

why.correct: Losing people and jobs, then demolishing empty houses, is the decline stage. The vacant land can later be reused.
options: Infilling adds buildings; here they were removed.
Detroit was built up long before; this is the later decline.
Right: decline leaves empty lots.
A shrinking city is not forming a new CBD.

items.q: A city's zoning allows only one detached house per lot on most of its residential land. What is the most likely effect?
options: Many new apartment towers in those neighborhoods
Low residential density across most neighborhoods
Factories built next to homes
Higher density at the city's edge than at its center

why.correct: If only single houses are allowed, apartments cannot be built there, so density stays low wherever that rule applies.
options: The rule forbids apartments in those zones.
Right: the rule locks in low density.
Zoning usually keeps factories apart from homes.
The rule affects most residential land; it does not reverse the usual pattern.

items.q: Houston, Texas, has no citywide zoning code. Which pattern would you most expect to see there?
options: Homes and stores mixed on some streets
Factories kept far from homes by a city law on land use
Buildings of about the same height on each block in the city
Very few new buildings since the city was first founded

why.correct: Without zoning, different land uses can locate next to each other wherever a builder chooses, though private deed rules limit some areas.
options: Right: without zoning, uses mix more freely.
Without zoning, no city law sets that separation.
Heights vary with land values and builders' choices.
Houston has grown a great deal.

items.q: Which of these are examples of infilling? Select all that apply.
options: Apartments built on an empty parking lot downtown
A new subdivision built on farmland 40 km from the city
A new office tower on a vacant lot between two old buildings
A highway built through open forest

why.correct: Infilling uses vacant or underused land inside an area already built up.
options: Right: an empty lot downtown is inside the built-up area.
Farmland at the edge is outside the built-up area: that is sprawl.
Right: a vacant lot between buildings is infill.
A highway through forest builds on open land.

items.q: Build an explanation of how one force shaped residential density in a named city.

specific.model: In Hong Kong, flat land is scarce and the government built many public housing towers, so most families live in high-rise apartments and residential density is very high.

place.label: City
options: Hong Kong
a crowded city

why.1: Name a real city: a vague place earns no credit.

cause.label: Force
options: flat land is scarce and the government built many public housing towers
most families own large houses with yards

why.1: Large houses with yards mean low density, the opposite of Hong Kong.

effect.label: Effect on density
options: most families live in high-rise apartments and residential density is very high
most families live on farms outside the city

why.1: The force named pushes people into towers, not onto farms.

why.correct: A full explanation names the city, the force and the link to density.
